Dear Information Governance Team,

Thank you for your response. To whom am I speaking?

I note your advice that Glamorgan Archives may be the appropriate
repository for historic material. I will contact Glamorgan Archives
separately.

However, I would like to clarify that my request was not limited to
deposited historical archive material.

My request concerns any recorded information held by Cardiff Council and
its predecessor authorities relating to Great House Farm, Llandough (Ty
Mawr), including operational records created or retained by the Council.

Please confirm:

Which Cardiff Council departments were consulted before reaching the
conclusion that Glamorgan Archives was the appropriate route;

Whether searches were carried out within:
- Planning records;
- Building Control records;
- Legal Services records;
- Estates/property records;
- Highways records;
- Environmental/archaeology records;
- Records inherited from former Glamorgan County Council or South Glamorgan
County Council;
- Whether the following search terms were used:

"Great House Farm"
"Ty Mawr"
"Llandough"
"Buckler"
"Williams"
"BP Properties"
"BP Pension Trust"
"Western Ground Rents"

Whether Cardiff Council holds any records relating to:
- the demolition of Great House Farm around 1988;
- planning and development of the replacement housing;
- any inspections, surveys, photographs or reports concerning the site;
- correspondence with BP, their representatives, the Buckler/Williams
family, Cadw, archaeological bodies or other public authorities.

I appreciate Glamorgan Archives may hold historic deposited collections.
However, an archive referral does not confirm whether Cardiff Council
itself holds related administrative records, and I would therefore be
grateful for confirmation of the searches undertaken before this request is
redirected.

Given the age and significance of the records concerned, I would appreciate
this clarification at your earliest convenience.

Kind regards,

Requester

objects.

Any records of associated human or animal remains from the same discovery,

Any related excavation, watching-brief, or discovery reports held by the

If any of the requested information is already publicly available (for

if you could simply provide the relevant accession numbers or catalogue
links.

seeking advice or opinion.

  *   whether they formed part of a wider inspection file;
  *   whether any inspection notes, recommendation forms, field notebooks, photographic registers or other associated records were created; and
  *   if such records once existed, whether they are now believed to have been destroyed.

  *   that Great House Farm was never considered for statutory protection;
  *   that it was considered, but the records no longer survive; or

Requester

records.transcript:
Ms Longford,

Thank you for your email.

I note your confirmation that Cadw holds no transfer lists, accession
records, archive schedules or other documentation recording whether records
relating to Great House Farm were transferred to the RCAHMW, and that Cadw
also holds no record of their destruction. I also note that the suggestion
that records may have been transferred or destroyed is based upon an
inspector's understanding of historic practice rather than documentary
evidence relating to this case.

However, there remain a small number of points on which I would be grateful
for clarification.

   1.

   The original response of 11 June stated that associated records "would
   have been either transferred to the RCAHMW or destroyed under the Public
   Records Act 1958". As no transfer or destruction documentation has been
   identified, on what evidential basis was that statement made?
   2.

   Does the Welsh Government now accept that it holds no documentary
   evidence that any records relating to Great House Farm were transferred to
   the RCAHMW?
   3.

   Contemporary press reports concerning the proposed protection of Great
   House Farm referred to consultation with other departments and bodies
   before a decision was reached. During this correspondence I therefore asked
   whether searches extended to correspondence with other departments,
   external bodies and related records. Although you have confirmed wider
   searches were undertaken, no such records have been identified. Could you
   therefore confirm whether the Welsh Government's position is that it holds
   no surviving correspondence, memoranda, consultation records or other
   documents relating to any such consultations concerning Great House Farm?
   4.

   Is the Welsh Government's position therefore that, apart from the two
   photographs dated 29 July 1988, no inspection report, recommendation,
   consultation correspondence, assessment, case file or associated
   documentation relating to the 1988 consideration of Great House Farm
   survives?

These questions are intended solely to clarify the historical record and to
reconcile the original response with the findings of the internal review.

Thank you for your assistance, and I look forward to your reply.

Yours sincerely,

Requester

> Dear Ms Longford,
>
> Thank you for your letter of 2 July 2026 responding to the internal review
> of my Freedom of Information request (ATISN 27021) concerning Great House
> Farm, Llandough.
>
> I appreciate the additional searches undertaken during the review and the
> explanation provided regarding the physical record series examined.
>
> However, having considered both the original response of 11 June 2026 and
> the outcome of the internal review, I would be be grateful if you could
> clarify a number of points which appear to remain unresolved.
>
> *1. Documentary basis of the original response*
>
> The original response stated that Great House Farm was visited and
> assessed by Cadw inspectors and that the building did not satisfy the
> statutory listing criteria.
>
> The internal review now confirms that no assessment, report or case file
> relating to that decision has been located and further states that any
> relevant file may have been destroyed before being entered onto the
> electronic records system.
>
> Please therefore identify the documentary basis upon which the original
> response concluded that the property was assessed and found not to meet the
> listing criteria.
>
> Specifically:
>
>    - Is that conclusion derived from a surviving record?
>    - If so, please identify that record.
>    - If not, please explain how that conclusion was reached.
>
> *2. The inspection of 29 July 1988*
>
> The original disclosure included two photographs dated 29 July 1988.
>
> Please confirm:
>
>    - whether those photographs were taken as part of a formal listing
>    inspection;
>    - whether they formed part of a wider inspection file;
>    - whether any inspection notes, recommendation forms, field notebooks,
>    photographic registers or other associated records were created; and
>    - if such records once existed, whether they are now believed to have
>    been destroyed.
>
> *3. Basis for the statement that records may have been destroyed*
>
> The review states that it is possible documentation dating from around
> 1988 was destroyed before being entered onto the electronic records system.
>
> Please clarify whether that statement is based upon:
>
>    - documentary evidence relating specifically to Great House Farm;
>    - records management documentation such as retention schedules,
>    destruction registers or disposal logs; or
>    - a general understanding of historic records management practices.
>
> If no destruction records exist for the relevant file series, please
> confirm this.
>
> *4. Scope of the searches*
>
> Please confirm whether searches extended beyond the registered listing
> files to include, where appropriate:
>
>    - ministerial correspondence;
>    - senior officials' correspondence;
>    - legal files;
>    - inspector's working papers;
>    - site visit records;
>    - archaeological or conservation files;
>    - policy records; and
>    - correspondence with external organisations, including the Vale of
>    Glamorgan Council, the former Welsh Office and other heritage bodies.
>
> If any of these categories were not searched, I would be grateful if you
> could identify which.
>
> *5. Welsh Government's position*
>
> Finally, I would be appreciate clarification of the Welsh Government's
> position regarding Great House Farm.
>
> Does the Welsh Government's position now amount to one of the following:
>
>    - that Great House Farm was never considered for statutory protection;
>    - that it was considered, but the records no longer survive; or
>    - that it is no longer possible to determine whether consideration
>    took place because the relevant records are unavailable?
>
> If none of those accurately reflects your position, I would be grateful if
> you could explain what the Welsh Government's position is.
>
> These questions arise directly from the original response and the internal
> review and are intended to clarify the historical record rather than seek
> the creation of new information.
>
> I look forward to your response.
>
> Yours sincerely,

records.transcript:
Dear Mr Haste,

Thank you for your letter of 30 July 2026 (reference N610CGV) and for
identifying the surviving records held in relation to titles WA231076 and
WA240304.

I am not seeking to reopen HM Land Registry’s complaints procedure or to
ask for any previous decision to be reconsidered. This is a separate
request for clarification arising from the additional information in your
letter.

Your letter is the first to set out in detail which first-registration
records survive. It therefore enables a number of factual questions that
could not previously be asked with precision.

First, earlier correspondence referred to a 1971 abstract of title having
been lodged with the first registration applications. That document does
not appear as a separate item in the schedule you have provided. Could you
please confirm whether:

the 1971 abstract of title survives as a separate document;

it forms part of one of the listed items (and if so, which); or

it is no longer held.

Second, earlier correspondence referred to a certificate given with the
first registration application in which the applicant’s solicitors stated
they were “not aware of any question or doubt affecting the title”. Your
schedule identifies the surviving first-registration application as Form 1E
(item 13 for WA231076). Could you please confirm whether that certificate
forms part of the surviving Form 1E, and if not, identify the surviving
document in which it appears.

The purpose of this enquiry is solely to establish what information is
actually contained in the surviving first-registration records you have
listed.

Could you therefore confirm whether those records — including the
first-registration application, the A13/DL list of documents lodged, the
correspondence with Linklaters & Paines, any related applications, and any
surviving examiner’s notes, file notes, memoranda or internal
correspondence — contain any reference to:

Mary Williams (also known as Mrs Buckler);

Fred Buckler;

Ty Mawr;

Great House Farm;

any assertion by another person that they owned, occupied, or claimed an
interest in the land;

any ownership dispute, possession proceedings, litigation, or competing
claim affecting the land;

any issue, doubt, objection, caution, competing interest, or other matter
affecting title.

In particular, could you confirm whether any of the surviving
first-registration records contain any indication that another party
asserted ownership of, or claimed an interest in, the land before first
registration was completed for either title.

If any such reference exists, please identify the document or item number
in which it appears.

If no such references appear anywhere in the surviving records, a simple
confirmation of that fact would be sufficient.

If these questions cannot be answered without inspection of the documents
themselves, please confirm that and identify which specific documents are
capable of answering them, so that any Form OC2 application can be limited
to those documents alone.

This request concerns only the factual contents of the records identified
in your letter of 30 July 2026.

Thank you for your assistance. I look forward to your reply.

Yours sincerely,


Requester 

 and Life Memeber

records.transcript:
Dear Patricia Reynolds,

Thank you for your response of 30 July 2026 (Case number CAS-343481-X5H3M6).

I note your advice that The National Archives is not the primary repository
for the material described in my original enquiry. However, my enquiry also
concerns whether The National Archives holds any recorded information
relating to the existence, transfer, retention, destruction, or absence of
such records.

Under the Freedom of Information Act 2000, I request confirmation of any
recorded information held by The National Archives relating to Great House
Farm / Ty Mawr, Llandough (Glamorgan), including historical references
under alternative descriptions such as Cedfin or equivalent contemporary
descriptions.

Specifically, please confirm whether The National Archives holds:

   1. *Manorial and estate records*

Any catalogue entries, Manorial Documents Register information, finding
aids, transfer records, or related documentation concerning:

   - the Manor of Llandough (Glamorgan);
   - pre-1667 references to occupants, customary tenants, holdings,
   surveys, rentals, terriers, or court rolls;
   - Vaughan family estate holdings at Llandough;
   - Great House Farm / Ty Mawr or any earlier description of the holding.

Please include any references to HMC9/311 or related archival series.

   2. *Records concerning disposal, destruction, or transfer of records*

Any recorded information showing:

   - whether records relating to Great House Farm, Llandough, the Bute
   Estate, Vaughan family papers, or associated land records were ever
   transferred to The National Archives;
   - whether any such records were destroyed, and if so:
      - what records were destroyed;
      - when they were destroyed;
      - under which retention schedule, disposal authority, or policy;
      - which body authorised or carried out the destruction.

If no such records are held, please confirm whether any disposal or
transfer records indicate that relevant material was never deposited or was
destroyed elsewhere.

   3. *Legal and court records*

Any central court records, indexes, correspondence, or administrative
records concerning:

   - possession or title disputes involving Great House Farm / Ty Mawr;
   - Western Ground Rents Ltd;
   - BP Pension Trust Ltd;
   - BP Properties Ltd;
   - Mountjoy Ltd;
   - the proceedings connected with *BP Properties Ltd v Buckler* [1987]
   EWCA Civ 2.


   4. *Estate transfers and ownership records*

Any government-held correspondence, files, or records relating to:

   - the Bute Estate;
   - the 1938 sale or transfer of Great House Farm;
   - Western Ground Rents Ltd acquisition;
   - BP Pension Trust/BP Properties involvement;
   - any government department involvement in the property.


   5. *Family correspondence and related records*

Any correspondence, reports, enquiries, or administrative records held by
The National Archives involving:

   - Mary Williams;
   - Fred Buckler;
   - William Buckler;
   - the Williams/Buckler family;
   - Great House Farm / Ty Mawr;
   - Bute Estate representatives;
   - Western Ground Rents;
   - BP entities.


   6. *1980–1988 period and demolition/eviction matters*

Any records concerning:

   - the public campaign regarding Great House Farm;
   - parliamentary correspondence or government enquiries;
   - the 1988 eviction/demolition;
   - Cadw or government communications;
   - European Commission of Human Rights Application 14464/88 (Buckler v
   United Kingdom).

If any relevant information is held, please provide catalogue references,
descriptions, and access arrangements.

If no relevant information is held, please confirm:

   - the searches undertaken;
   - the catalogues, databases, and record series searched;
   - whether any relevant records were ever held and subsequently
   transferred, destroyed, or disposed of.

I am pursuing parallel enquiries with the National Library of Wales,
Glamorgan Archives and other repositories. This request is specifically
directed at recorded information held by The National Archives.

Yours sincerely,

Requester

Dear Sir/Madam,

This is a separate Freedom of Information request under the Freedom of
Information Act 2000.

It is distinct from my earlier request under your reference 260607013
(submitted 7 June 2026), which concerned the location and access options
for historical court records relating to Great House Farm, Mary
Williams/Buckler, Western Ground Rents and BP (focusing on the 1915, 1955
and 1962 possession proceedings and title/equitable interest evidence).

This new request is limited solely to records of the hearing (or hearings)
at Barry Magistrates Court in late January 1989 at which the Crown
Prosecution Service withdrew the charge arising from the allegation of 29
April 1988 as being “out of time.”

I write under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 to request recorded
information relating to criminal proceedings involving *William Beverly
("Billy") Buckler* arising from events connected with the eviction and
demolition of *Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan*,
during 1988–1989.

I am seeking administrative and recorded information concerning the
handling of these proceedings, rather than personal data contained within
individual case files.

Specifically, I request copies of, or access to, any recorded information
held concerning:

   1.

   The prosecution in which a charge dating from *29 April 1988* alleging
   threatening words or behaviour was withdrawn because the proceedings were
   considered *"out of time."*
   2.

   Any records identifying:
   - the court in which that decision was made;
      - the date of the hearing;
      - the prosecutor involved (reported contemporaneously as *Mr Jeff
      Clarke*);
      - the legal basis upon which the summons was determined to be out of
      time.
   3.

   Records relating to Billy Buckler's appearances before the courts
during *January–March
   1989*, including any surviving:
   - cause lists;
      - court registers;
      - hearing lists;
      - minute books;
      - court log books;
      - bench records;
      - administrative case records;
      - listing records;
      - prosecution correspondence;
      - disposal records; or similar recorded information.
   4.

   Records concerning the proceedings heard in *Cardiff on or about 23
   March 1989*, including recorded information showing:
   - the charges before the court;
      - which charges were proceeded with;
      - which charges were withdrawn or discontinued;
      - the sentence imposed;
      - any recorded fine;
      - any credit given for time already spent in custody.
   5.

   Records concerning charges arising from the *November 1988 eviction of
   Great House Farm*, including allegations of assault and wanton and
   furious driving.
   6.

   Any recorded information concerning:
   - remand or custody records;
      - warrants;
      - bail conditions;
      - injunction-related court administration;
      - any order restricting Billy Buckler from approaching Great House
      Farm.
   7.

   Any retention, destruction or disposal records relating to the above
   court files, including:
   - destruction schedules;
      - retention schedules;
      - disposal certificates;
      - archive transfer records;
      - accession records;
      - file movement records;
      - records identifying when and under what authority any files were
      destroyed or transferred.
   8.

   Any file references, case numbers, register entries or archive
   references relating to these proceedings, even where the substantive files
   no longer survive.

If any of the requested information has been transferred to another body,
such as the relevant archive service or another part of HM Courts &
Tribunals Service or the Ministry of Justice, please identify the receiving
body and any known reference numbers.

If any information is withheld, please specify the exemption relied upon,
explain why it applies, and disclose all reasonably segregable information.

If some parts of this request are more readily available than others, I

Regards,


Requester
